data.notes:
Migration: Belonging, Dwelling and Laboring. Shan Yang, Post-MA Fellow, The American University in Cairo.

Description: This seminar engages contemporary questions of migration. It explores the global movement of people and their lifeworlds as migrants, refugees and asylum-seekers. It introduces students to critical work about mobilities, citizenship and developmentalism through examining the effects of these strategies on practices of belonging, dwelling and laboring in the everyday.

Requirements: 1. Class attendance. 2. Read readings assigned each week.

Reading schedule note: All texts will be shared through Dropbox.

The flow's footnote thanks Dr. Martina Rieker, whose graduate seminar Mobilities: Gender and Migration at the American University in Cairo the syllabus is mainly derived from.
